questions.q: What is Project 1, as scoped in this lesson?
options: A production-pattern RAG knowledge assistant over a document set the student chooses
A multi-tenant SaaS product serving many customers' document sets
A fine-tuned custom language model trained from scratch
A frontend-only chat widget with no retrieval or generation
questions.explain: The lesson scopes Project 1 as a production-pattern retrieval-augmented generation assistant over a real document set the student picks themselves — not a multi-tenant product or a fine-tuned model.

questions.q: Which of the following is explicitly listed as OUT of scope for this project?
options: Retrieval of relevant chunks for a question
A hand-built evaluation set
Fine-tuning an embedding or language model
A containerized deployment behind a minimal API
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly excludes a custom auth system, multi-tenant isolation, fine-tuning any model, a polished frontend, and autoscaling — retrieval, evaluation, and deployment are all in scope.

questions.q: What library does this lesson name for chunking, in the stack for Lesson 4?
options: pandas' built-in string split method
A custom regular expression with no library
The Qdrant client's internal chunker
langchain_text_splitters' RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
questions.explain: The lesson's stack names langchain_text_splitters' RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter as the tool for overlap-aware chunking, built out fully in Lesson 4.

questions.q: Which vector database does this lesson's stack use for storing embeddings?
options: Qdrant, the same vector database this path's RAG & Vector Databases course covered
A plain SQLite file with no vector support
No vector database is used in this project
Spreadsheet software
questions.explain: The lesson names Qdrant as the vector-storage layer, reusing the same database already covered in this path's RAG & Vector Databases course.

questions.q: Why does the recommended repository layout put eval/ in its own folder, separate from rag/?
options: Because Python forbids importing across folders
To keep evaluation as a clearly separated concern from retrieval and generation, which a reviewer notices
Because the eval folder is never actually used in this project
There is no stated reason in the lesson
questions.explain: The lesson frames the separate folders as keeping concerns clearly separated — an organizational choice a reviewer is likely to notice, not a technical requirement of the language.
